choices.A: A triangle with one angle measuring 90 degrees
choices.B: A square with sides of equal length
choices.C: A circle (note: circles have infinite lines of rotational symmetry, but no reflection symmetry)

questions.solution: A square has four lines of reflection symmetry running through its center and connecting opposite vertices. This makes option B the correct choice. The other options either have no reflection symmetry (circle), only one line of symmetry (triangle), or are not symmetrical at all (parallelogram).
questions.explanation: Reflection symmetry refers to a shape that can be divided into two identical halves by a line or plane.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing C, as some might think a circle has no reflection symmetry. However, a circle actually has infinite lines of rotational symmetry but not reflection symmetry.

questions.stem: Does the following figure have rotational symmetry? If yes, how many degrees does it rotate to match its original position?
questions.solution: The figure is a regular hexagon, which has rotational symmetry of 360 degrees. It can be rotated in a full circle and still match its original position. Therefore, the correct answer is D.
questions.explanation: Rotational symmetry refers to a shape that looks the same after rotating around its center by a certain angle.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B or C, as some might think it has only 90-degree or 180-degree rotational symmetry. However, a regular hexagon can be rotated in increments of 60 degrees up to a full rotation.

questions.stem: Identify the line(s) of symmetry for this letter: A
questions.solution: The letter 'A' has no lines of symmetry. None of the options provided accurately describe its symmetry properties.
questions.explanation: Lines of symmetry refer to a line that divides a shape into two identical halves when reflected across it.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or B, as some might mistakenly think there is symmetry in the letter 'A.' However, it does not have any lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: Which figure has both reflection and rotational symmetry?

choices.B: A rectangle with opposite sides parallel
choices.C: An equilateral triangle with equal sides
choices.D: A parallelogram with one pair of parallel sides

questions.solution: A rectangle has both reflection symmetry (two horizontal and two vertical lines) and rotational symmetry (180 degrees). The other options either lack reflection symmetry or have only rotational symmetry.
questions.explanation: Both reflection and rotational symmetries can be present in a shape, meaning it can be divided into identical halves by a line or plane and also looks the same after being rotated around its center.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing C, as some might think an equilateral triangle has both symmetries. However, it only has rotational symmetry of 120 degrees.

questions.stem: Does a regular pentagon have reflection symmetry?

choices.C: It depends on the size of the pentagon
choices.D: It depends on the orientation of the pentagon

questions.solution: A regular pentagon has no reflection symmetry. It only has rotational symmetry.
questions.explanation: Reflection symmetry requires a shape to be identical after being reflected across a line, and a regular pentagon does not have this property.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, as some might think that because it's symmetrical, there must be reflection symmetry. However, the only symmetries present in a regular pentagon are rotational.

questions.stem: Which shape has the most lines of reflection symmetry?
questions.solution: A dodecagon (12-sided polygon) has 12 lines of reflection symmetry, more than a square (4), hexagon (6), or decagon (2).
questions.explanation: The number of lines of reflection symmetry in a regular polygon is equal to the number of sides it has.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, B, or C, as some might think that more complex shapes have fewer lines of symmetry. However, the number of lines increases with the number of sides.

questions.stem: Identify the type of symmetry exhibited by this figure: a circle with a dot in the center.
questions.solution: The figure has only rotational symmetry, as it can be rotated around its center without changing appearance. The dot in the center does not affect this property.
questions.explanation: Rotational symmetry refers to a shape that looks the same after being rotated around its center by a certain angle.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or C, as some might think there is reflection symmetry due to the dot. However, the dot does not create any lines of reflection symmetry.
